units.note: Greek of the second sentence-pair (to de, par' hois he pege...) is elliptical with no verb; English supplies 'astonishing ... succeed against'. Acceptable but the ellipsis is the editor's inference.
Numbers checked: 72 years, 44 reigned, four sons - all match.

findings.quote: They tried to prevent Antiochus from sailing along the coast
findings.problem: The Greek fragment opens with an ellipsis ('Res Asiae...') and then an infinitive clause, 'kolyein de ton Antiochon parapleein'; the finite subject and governing verb are lost. English supplies 'They tried' as if the sentence were whole (smoothed lacuna). The subject (who 'they' are) is not in the Greek.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] to prevent Antiochus from sailing along the coast

units.note: Fragment begins mid-sentence in the Greek.
Marcus = the consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus (Greek: epi Markellou Klaudiou hypatou ... Markos).
Numbers checked: 1000 talents, half at once, half over ten years; five vessels plus the sixteen-banked ship - match.

findings.quote: And in their cleverness in arguing against one another, these speakers immediately gave themselves away.
findings.problem: Greek: kai toutous eutheos epedeiknysan autoi kath' hauton dia tes pros allelous heuresilogias. 'toutous' (masc. acc.) refers to the places just mentioned (the retained ones of lesser appearance); the speakers themselves pointed out these very places, to their own detriment (kath' hauton), through their ingenuity in debating with one another. English drops the object and turns it into a vague 'gave themselves away'.
findings.proposed_fix: And these very places they themselves immediately pointed out, to their own cost, through their ingenuity in arguing with one another.

units.note: The reference of 'toutous' and of kath' hauton is somewhat ambiguous in the Greek; low confidence. Also noted, not flagged: 'strategos hypatos' (Titus) is rendered 'proconsul and commander'; the Greek literally pairs 'general' and 'consul', but Titus's imperium was proconsular in 196, so the rendering is defensible.
